oil.summary: Crude suffered its sharpest single-session collapse in months, with Brent off 6.26% to $92.17 and WTI down 4.90% to $86.38, as diplomatic optimism swamped supply-side risk. Qatar's prime minister carried an Iranian interim deal proposal to the White House, and unconfirmed reports of a broader U.S.-Iran diplomatic breakthrough drove the rout, more than offsetting a confirmed attack on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and overnight Ukrainian drone strikes on Russia's second-largest oil refinery. RBOB gasoline led the complex lower, shedding 5.15% on the day and 20.07% over the month. The market is essentially pricing a Hormuz reopening premium out of the curve. CME options now imply a 77% probability of an OPEC cut at the May 2026 meeting, suggesting the market expects the group to defend price. Traders are also sidestepping Russian diesel following the Trump-Putin arrangement, further muddying Atlantic Basin flows.
drivers: Iran diplomatic breakthrough hopes: Qatar PM carried Iranian Hormuz interim deal proposal to White House, triggering broad risk-off for geopolitical premium
Saudi East-West pipeline attacked and Ukrainian drones struck Russia's second-largest refinery, but supply-disruption fear was overpowered by peace optimism
CME OPEC Watch pricing 77% chance of a production cut at May 2026 meeting, signalling market expects OPEC response to price slide

gas.summary: Henry Hub rebounded sharply, gaining 6.90% to $3.205/MMBtu on the day and extending a 12.22% weekly gain, as global LNG market tightness underpinned sentiment. A published analysis flagged LNG spot prices above $30/MMBtu heading into winter 2026/27, characterising the season as one of extreme uncertainty. Geopolitical cross-currents added to the anxiety: Russian strikes continued to target Ukrainian energy infrastructure, while Israel's Energy Ministry awarded six offshore gas exploration licenses near Leviathan to Murphy Oil and Ratio Energies, a signal of longer-term Eastern Mediterranean supply ambitions. The Saudi pipeline attack added a marginal risk bid. On a one-month basis Henry Hub is essentially flat (-0.47%), so today's move looks like a weather- and LNG-premium catch-up rather than a structural shift.
drivers: Global LNG spot prices above $30/MMBtu and deep winter supply uncertainty providing a strong floor and driving the 6.90% single-day surge
Ongoing Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure sustaining European supply-security anxiety
Israel awards six Leviathan-area offshore gas licenses to Murphy Oil and Ratio Energies, adding longer-term Eastern Med supply optionality

power.summary: EU carbon EUAs edged up 0.96% to €83.42/EUA, holding near the top of a one-month range that is roughly flat (+0.68%) despite a 3.17% weekly pullback. The incremental support came from European power prices jumping to their highest level since 2022, driven by still and cloudy weather curtailing wind and solar output across major continental markets. Russian air strikes targeting Ukraine's power grid ahead of Abu Dhabi peace talks forced Ukrainian authorities to scramble power restoration for hundreds of thousands in the east, adding geopolitical anxiety. A separate analysis on AI-driven electricity demand growth flagged potential structural upside for baseload consumption. LNG tightness above $30/MMBtu adds an additional cost floor for gas-fired generation, feeding through to power prices and indirectly supporting carbon.
drivers: Wind and solar generation slump in key European markets drove power prices to 2022 highs, tightening the carbon-power price correlation
Russian strikes on Ukraine's power grid ahead of Abu Dhabi peace talks amplified regional energy security concerns
LNG spot prices above $30/MMBtu lifting gas-fired generation costs and providing an indirect floor for EU carbon allowances
